details.value:
Sermons by Beernt Arborstier, Parts II and III.
	•	f. IIIv: Table of contents of this Book of Various Sermons.
	•	ff. IIIv–153v: This first sermon is on a penitential life or a cloistered spiritual life
(Book of Various Sermons, 21 sermons, Beernt Arborstier),
inc. “Ic sel opclymmen op den palmboem ende ic sel gripen sine vruchte …”
	•	ff. 153v–154r: Table of contents of the following sermons.
	•	ff. 154r–219v (=221v): This first [sermon] is on the Finding of the Holy Cross
(This is the third part of the sermons, 9 sermons, Beernt Arborstier),
inc. “Die my vint die vint dat leuen ende sel heyl sceppen vanden heren …”

details.value:
Stuttgart, Württembergische Landesbibliothek, HB XVII 17, The writer has also written her name at the top of each page. On 227 r there is also a coat of arms in addition to her name, which is exceptionally placed at the beginning of the layer in the lower edge of the page: red field with a recessed chevron left in the parchment background and three quinces (?) in yellow ( Schraut , Fig. 5);
 
 An Alheid called Quidenbomen is documented as abbess of the Cistercian monastery Marienborn (Eckartshausen, district of Büdingen) in 1339-1342 (Hessisches Urkundenbuch 2, edited by Heinrich Reimer (Publications from the Imperial Prussian State Archives 51) Leipzig 1892, p. 523f.No ...​​​​​ ​1777, p. 183 No. 131; for monastery history see Simon ibid., vol. 1, pp. 109-117, and Georg Wilhelm Justin Wagner , The former spiritual monasteries in the Grand Duchy of Hesse 1, Darmstadt 1873, pp. 199-210) .

details.value:
Alijt van Hyell, Deventer, Colophon, High, Deventer, Athenaeumbibliotheek, 101 A 34 KL, Five sheets with writing exercises by Deventer girls, one of them dated 1586. The texts are probably copies of Deventer archive documents. Sheet a: Two writing exercises by Alijt van Hyell (?). - page b: Two writing exercises by Elsa Luickens (?). - page c: Writing exercise (copy of charter mayors, aldermen and council of Deventer) by Jenneken van Brijell (?). - page d: Writing exercise by Janneken Tijers (?). - page e: Writing exercise by Maria van Appeldoorn
Paper, 5 sheets (2 folded and 3 cut), sheet a: 395×273 mm, sheet b: 444×320 mm, sheets ce (cut): 195×315 mm. - At least two leaves served as maculature

details.value:
Angela Varnbühler, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

details.value:
Horarium with prayers in Swedish (Dorothea Nilsdotter's prayer book)

1 (ff. 1r – 8v ) Holy Trinity times
Title: None
2 (ff. (1r – 1v) ) Holy Trinity Times: On the benefit of Holy Trinity Times
Title: None
Incipit: That was a sorrow … I will take it there until the end of time.
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , pp. 7–8.
3 (ff. (2r – 8v) ) Prayers to the Holy Trinity: From the times of the Holy Trinity (7 + final prayer)
Title: None
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , pp. 9–13.
4 (ff. 8v – 10r ) Prayers to the Holy Trinity (7 prayers)
Title: Here comes the third person, please pray for me
Incipit: Loff hedher, oc ära wari tik alzwaldogher gudh
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , pp. 14–16.
5 (ff. 10r – 13v ) Prayer for the protection of God, the Virgin Mary and the angels (4 points)
Title: A good prayer for the Holy Trinity
Incipit: O alzwaldogher gudh fadher hwilkin som wilde kalla thin son mz tässom hælga nampnom
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , pp. 462–465.
6 (ff. 13v – 15v ) Prayer to S. Erasmus: variant b (= a but with a different heading)
Title: What man has read these verses, and what is written?
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , p. 403.
7 (ff. 15v – 16v ) ​​Pope Leo III (attributed), Prayer to the Holy Cross (incl.: Our Lord Jesus Holy Cross be with me)
Title: A good prayer for your holy cross
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , pp. 202–203.
8 (ff. 16v – 17v ) Birgitta Birgersdotter , St. Birgitta's prayer for help against the power of sin and the devil
Rubric: This is the written word, the prayer, the mother, and the daily reading of Saint Birgitta
24 (ff. 31r – 32v ) Mechtild of Hackeborn (Mechtildis de Hackeborn), "Three Woes" ​​about assistance at the hour of death (from Revelations: book 1, chapter 86)
Title: Sancta mäktildher bathed to the Virgin Mary and among other prayers
Editions: Geete (1899) , pp. 181–182; Geete (1899) , pp. 390–392.
32 (ff. 43r – 44r ) Prayer on the five wounds of Christ (Bön till Jesu fem sår): Added first stanza
Rubric: Sanctus Gregorius gave all those who read prayers to the poor and needy [...] never get half-witted, God gave them the
33 (ff. 44r – 45r ) Antiphon: The angel Gabriel was sent to the virgin Mary, espoused to Joseph
Title: None
34 (ff. 45r – 45v ) Oratio/preces (prayer/prayers in Latin)
Rubric: what man reads the prayer written by the apostle […] [ f. 45v ] And he scolds [!] his soul from the devil's forest
It begins: [ f. 45v ] O Virgin Mary, I beseech you through the Father whose power has overshadowed you.
35 (ff. 45v – 46r ) Ave Sanctissima Maria, mater Dei, Regina caeli (Prayer to the Virgin Mary before her image)
Heading: Til thenna æpther skriffna bøn gaff paffwe [ f. 46r ] sixtus then fiärdhe xj M aar afflat
36 (ff. 46r – 47r ) Prayer to St. Andrew
Title: A good prayer for them that glorify the Lord, Saint Andrew the Apostle
Starts: Saint Andrew's wars
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , p. 381.
37 (ff. 47r – 47v ) Bön till S. Katarina av Alexandria: variant b
Title: A prayer to the glorious virgin Saint Catherine of Greece
Begins: O glorious virgin and martyr Saint Catherine
Editions: Geete (1907-1909) , p. 421.
38 (f. 48r ) Oratio/preces (prayer/prayers in Latin)
Rubric: The highest written piece should be read from the top of your bed.
Begins: The sign of the Savior Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews, have mercy on me, a sinner.
39 (ff. 48r – 49r ) (Five incantations in verse for protection against enemies and evil to be read before going to bed)
Rubric: He who reads the tæssin æpther skriffna wærs før æn [ f. 48v ] he gets j sænggh tha skal ey owinen nalkas them stathenom
Begins: May this house be blessed enough.
40 (f. (48v)) Versus
Title: With another verse, sign the doors
Begins: Let the door be closed so that no evil may enter.
41 (f. (48v)) Versus
Category: There next to the beds
Begins: We together to the place, bless God, oh, the one who has created it.
42 (f. (48v)) Versus
Rubric: Sidhan alt hwsit
It begins: O Christ, blessed be this place, at your hour.
43 (ff. (48v–49r)) Versus
Rubrik: Thenna verse read three times mz korsens tekn ower alt hwsit
It begins: Through this sign of the cross may all evil flee far away.
102 (ff. 132r – 150v ) Seven penitential psalms with litany
Title: None
Begins: Let them blush and be troubled.
103 (f. (149r) ) Prayer: Hear, we beseech you, O Lord, our supplicatory prayers and
Title: None
104 (f. (149r) ) Prayer: Show us your ineffable mercy, O Lord.
Title: None
105 (ff. (149r – 150v) ) Prayer: By your mercy, we beseech you, O Lord, to free our
Title: None
106 (ff. 150v – 158v ) Office of the Holy Spirit (Hours of the Holy Spirit)
Title: None
107 (f. (158v) ) Prayer: God, who from the womb of the blessed Virgin Mary sent forth your word
Title: None

details.value:
Barbara Rutzin, Nuremberg, Script comparison, Medium, Nuremberg, Germanisches Nationalmuseum , Hs 114263b, Bastarda script by 9 hands:
 1. fols. 1r–48r, 48v–72r, 125r–131r: Cecilia Rotin (Schneider I, fig. 11)
 2. fols. 48rv, 120r–124v, 144v–145r: probably Hand 1 (ibid., fig. 12)
 3. fols. 60v, 72v, 131v–135r: Dorothea Schurstabin (ibid., fig. 9)
 4. fols. 73r–112v
 5. fols. 112v–119r: Barbara Rutzin (ibid., fig. 5)
 6. fols. 131v–132r
 7. fols. 136r–143r
 8. fols. 146r–156v
 9. fols. 145v, 157r–180r: Hand 3 (ibid., fig. 14)

Paper analysis by G. Piccard suggests the likely writing dates: fols. 1–156 between 1429–1432; fols. 157–180 between 1452–1455.

details.value:
Barbara von Rottenburg, Reuthin, Script comparison, Medium, Stuttgart, Württembergische Landesbibliothek, Brev. 63, Writer of the main parts: Sister Barbara von Rottenburg in the Dominican monastery Maria-Reut(h)in (Fiala/Irtenkauf p. 84)
Based on the documents used for binding, this (collective) manuscript originates from the Dominican convent of Reutin. According to G. Piccard’s watermark analysis, it was not begun before 1515 and was completed by around 1529.
The main scribe of its primary sections is Sister Barbara von Rottenburg of Reutin (Gand No. 175), who identifies herself in a manuscript she authored (Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 31, f.64r). She is considered the primary scribe of Reutin from around 1488 to 1534. Her works include:
 • Cod. theol. et phil. qu. 77 (1488-1492),
 • Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 31 (1492),
 • Cod. brev. 27 (1511),
 • Cod. brev. 73 (1521),
 • Cod. theol. et phil. qu. 49a-b (1524),
 • Cod. brev. 49 (1529),
 • Cod. theol. et phil. oct. 33 (1534).

details.value:
Barbara von Rottenburg, Reuthin, Script comparison, Medium, Stuttgart, Württembergische Landesbibliothek, Brev. 72, Bastarda currens script by several hands
An analysis of the watermarks by G. Piccard suggests a probable period of inscription between 1490-1492. The Dominican litany (119v) and the German rubrics written by a second, later hand (e.g., “Barbara von Rottenburg,” see Cod. brev. 63) indicate its origin in the Dominican convent of Reutin.

details.value:
Prayer book:
 • 57r–71r: Passion prayers beginning “Protect me at all times and especially at my last departure…” including (on 59r) a list of saints predominantly of Dominican origin.
70r: Morning prayer addressed to Eternal Wisdom: “O most beautiful, most radiant, eternal Wisdom…”
 • 71v–83v: Prayers to saints including Mary Magdalene, (76r) Anna, (78r) George, (79r) Nicholas, (80r) Dorothea, (80v) Barbara, (81v) Margaret, (82v) Catherine. At 83v, the date mentioned earlier is repeated.
 • 88r–100v: Prayer by St. Bernard when Jesus descended to him from the Cross: “Hail, Jesus, the salvation of the world…”
 • 101r: Blank.
 • 101v: Rubric for the Rosary of Christ, incomplete.
 • 142r–153v: Exhortation for the contemplation of the sovereignty of God, German, ,

details.value:
Barbara von Rottenburg, Reuthin, Colophon, High, Stuttgart, Württembergische Landesbibliothek, Brev. 73, several hands: Hd. 2 = Barbara von Rottenburg
The manuscript is composed of partially incomplete prayer booklets written by various hands at different times. The initial section was written in 1496 at the Benedictine Monastery of Lorch: “56v Written in Lorch in the year 1496 by Clemens of the convent brothers of Lorch” (likely Clemens Aurifabri, prior in 1490; see Württembergische Geschichtsquellen, Vol. 12, 1910, p. 86).
The second hand is attributed to Sister Barbara of Rottenburg from Reutin (see Cod.brev.63), suggesting Reutin as the manuscript’s library of origin. Her work is dated to 1521 (83v).

Cecilia Rotin, Nuremberg, Script comparison, Medium, Nuremberg, Germanisches Nationalmuseum , Hs 114263b, Bastarda script by 9 hands:
 1. fols. 1r–48r, 48v–72r, 125r–131r: Cecilia Rotin (Schneider I, fig. 11)
 2. fols. 48rv, 120r–124v, 144v–145r: probably Hand 1 (ibid., fig. 12)
 3. fols. 60v, 72v, 131v–135r: Dorothea Schurstabin (ibid., fig. 9)
 4. fols. 73r–112v
 5. fols. 112v–119r: Barbara Rutzin (ibid., fig. 5)
 6. fols. 131v–132r
 7. fols. 136r–143r
 8. fols. 146r–156v
 9. fols. 145v, 157r–180r: Hand 3 (ibid., fig. 14)

Paper analysis by G. Piccard suggests the likely writing dates: fols. 1–156 between 1429–1432; fols. 157–180 between 1452–1455.

details.value: Cecilia Sparnecker, Germany, Colophon, High, Würzburg Universitätsbibliothek, M.ch.f.4, A collection of manuscripts, written primarily on paper, which can be localized to Bamberg. The first part of the manuscript contains a German mirror of salvation. Erasmus Sternhals is identified as its writer in a colophon. The work was probably made for the Bamberg canon Georg von Löwenstein. This is indicated by the depiction of a kneeling canon and several coats of arms on f.56r. The German-language biography of the Holy Bishop Otto, which is bound in afterwards, also refers to Bamberg. It was written down by two Bamberg Poor Clares and completed in 1483. The third work in the collection is a life of Saint Catherine, dated 1488 and also written by a woman.

details.value: Christina Kamrer, Nuremberg, Colophon, High, Gera, HB 7623, In the period after the introduction of the reform, Engelthal received a German martyrology from the Nuremberg St. Catherine's Monastery, which Sister Christina Kamrerin completed on October 28, 1518. She wrote it for the prioress Birgitta Haller and the convent. The manuscript is now in the Gera City Archives (HB 7623) and was made known by Antje Willing: The Library of the St. Catherine's Monastery in Nuremberg. Synoptic Representation of the Book Lists Vol. 1 (2012), p. LXXXII (see also http://www.handschriftencensus.de/10308 with a link to the archive description by Paul Sparmberg).

Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, BnF Français 1176, f.36v
 Le ms. Français 1176 est un des vingt-cinq manuscrits entièrement copiés de la main de Christine de Pizan. Selon l’ Album Christine de Pizan, ce manuscrit est le plus ancien témoin du texte, daté de 1405. 
 
 Corrections de la main de Christine de Pizan : additions indiquées dans la marge et rapportées dans l'interligne (f.58) ; additions avec signes de renvoi (f.20v, 43, 63) ; au f.76, préparation de la rubrique en écriture cursive. Nombreux mots, souvent déjà exponctués, barrés de rouge. Au verso de la 3e garde de parchemin, table de l'ouvrage ajoutée à l'encre rouge de la main de l'auteur.
One hand was identified as Christine's autograph by G. Ouy et C. Reno

details.value: Christine of Pizan, Paris, One hand was identified as Christine's autograph by G. Ouy et C. Reno., Medium, Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, BnF Français 835, Les manuscrits de Christine de Pizan ont été écrits par trois mains bien reconnaissables : P, R et X (Christine de Pizan elle-même). Le ms Français 835 a été transcrit, dans sa majeure partie par R, identifié à P. de Cruce : cf.Delsaux, « Profil d’un copiste des manuscrits originaux de Christine de Pisan : P. de La Croix, alias la main R », article à paraître dans Scriptorium. P a copié les ff.441vb, l. 26 à 44vb. La main X a fait quelques corrections : mouche ou restauration sur laquelle l’auteur a réécrit, à l’encre noire, les mots manquants au f.100 : cf.G. Ouy et C. Reno, « Identification des autographes de Christine de Pizan », dans Scriptorium, 34, 1980, p. 221-238.

Claricia, Augsburg, The Claricia Psalter takes its name from one of the initials, which depicts a young girl in secular dress swinging from the initial "Q," who has "Claricia" written around her head. It has been suggested that the image represents a novice artist who signed her work, but there are many other theories, and none are certain.

details.value:
Cordula von Schönau, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

details.value:
Dorothea Schurstabin, Nuremberg, Script comparison, Medium, Nuremberg, Germanisches Nationalmuseum , Hs 114263b, Bastarda script by 9 hands:
 1. fols. 1r–48r, 48v–72r, 125r–131r: Cecilia Rotin (Schneider I, fig. 11)
 2. fols. 48rv, 120r–124v, 144v–145r: probably Hand 1 (ibid., fig. 12)
 3. fols. 60v, 72v, 131v–135r: Dorothea Schurstabin (ibid., fig. 9)
 4. fols. 73r–112v
 5. fols. 112v–119r: Barbara Rutzin (ibid., fig. 5)
 6. fols. 131v–132r
 7. fols. 136r–143r
 8. fols. 146r–156v
 9. fols. 145v, 157r–180r: Hand 3 (ibid., fig. 14)

Paper analysis by G. Piccard suggests the likely writing dates: fols. 1–156 between 1429–1432; fols. 157–180 between 1452–1455.

details.value: East Anglian possible nun 1, Similar hands to other manuscripts associated with Norfolk nunneries: scribe II may also be the hand responsible for Cambridge UL MS Hh.I.11, f.45r-53v, 55r-60r. D. details.value: Elisabeth Eychelberger, Bamberg, Colophon, High, Würzburg Universitätsbibliothek, M.ch.f.4, A collection of manuscripts, written primarily on paper, which can be localized to Bamberg. The first part of the manuscript contains a German mirror of salvation. Erasmus Sternhals is identified as its writer in a colophon. The work was probably made for the Bamberg canon Georg von Löwenstein. This is indicated by the depiction of a kneeling canon and several coats of arms on f.56r. The German-language biography of the Holy Bishop Otto, which is bound in afterwards, also refers to Bamberg. It was written down by two Bamberg Poor Clares and completed in 1483. The third work in the collection is a life of Saint Catherine, dated 1488 and also written by a woman.

details.value: Scribe identified by notes on fols. 109r (el), 190v (eis), 222r (soror Elisabet):

Elisabeth Muntprat, St. Gallen, Colophon, High, Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Cgm 5233, 273 sheets (bound together from 2 parts: I: sheets 1-106; II: sheets 107-273)
	1.	First hand: from 107r, line 14 to 222r, and from 239r to 273r. The scribe identifies herself:
	•	109r: “el”, 190v: “eis”, 222r: “soror Elisabeth” – identified as Elisabeth Muntpratin the Elder (1459–1531), a member of the Dominican convent of St. Katharina in St. Gallen from 1472.
	•	See CMD-CH 3, Text volume, p. 34, no. 86; p. 101f., no. 285; p. 288 for more manuscripts and literature attributed to her, with figures 440 and 442.
	2.	Second hand: 222v–225v.
	3.	Third hand: 107r, lines 1–13, and 227r–238v.

details.value:
Elisabeth Muntprat, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

details.value:
Elsa Luickens, Deventer, Colophon, High, Deventer, Athenaeumbibliotheek, 101 A 34 KL, Five sheets with writing exercises by Deventer girls, one of them dated 1586. The texts are probably copies of Deventer archive documents. Sheet a: Two writing exercises by Alijt van Hyell (?). - page b: Two writing exercises by Elsa Luickens (?). - page c: Writing exercise (copy of charter mayors, aldermen and council of Deventer) by Jenneken van Brijell (?). - page d: Writing exercise by Janneken Tijers (?). - page e: Writing exercise by Maria van Appeldoorn
Paper, 5 sheets (2 folded and 3 cut), sheet a: 395×273 mm, sheet b: 444×320 mm, sheets ce (cut): 195×315 mm. - At least two leaves served as maculature

details.value: Les Enluminures attributed it to this scribe

It is possible that although the manuscript was decorated by Elsbeth Töpplin, it may have been copied for use at a house for friars (or monks), since the rubric on f. 30v in the Gospel reading for Holy Thursday mentions “fratribus” (the brothers).  An alternative and probably more likely explanation is that this was copied from an exemplar for Friars without updating the rubrics to reflect feminine use, even though it was used by the sisters at the convent of St. Mary Magdalene.

details.value:
Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, BnF Latin 7560, Des annotations et corrections interlinéaires sans doute de la main de la copiste : f.4r, 5r, 33r-34r, 39r, 42r, 44r, 46v-54r ; et d’autres mains : f.41r-43v, 47r-47v. Des annotations marginales de diverses mains : au f.1r, la cote Colbert, la cote Regius répétée deux fois, la cote actuelle, une ligne d’un chant religieux (« Nunctio uere quia misit dominus angelimi »), et des neumes (orisci catalans et neumes aquitains ; on en trouve aussi au f.54v) ; d’autres annotations à connotation religieuse sont à noter aux f.6r, 42v et 54v ; un certain nombre d’annotations sont illisibles ou effacées (f.11r, 22r, 40r et 54r) ; on peut également mentionner un astérisque au f.45r, un « y » au f.49r et, d’une main moderne, « 307 » sur le f.54v. 
 Comme l’indiquent C. Jeudy (1974, p. 129-130) et B. Bischoff (2014, p. 128-129) dans leur notice respective, le manuscrit a été copié dans le troisième quart du IXe siècle en France, dans un scriptorium d’influence insulaire, par une copiste du nom d’Eugenia, qui donne son nom dans une souscription rédigée en lettres grecques (mais en langue latine) au f.54r (voir H. OMONT, 1905, p. 15 pour la transposition). Il a peut-être été copié dans le Sud de la France ou en Catalogne, ou du moins s’y est trouvé très vite après sa copie, car la main légèrement postérieure à la première (fin du IXe siècle) qui ajoute les carmina des f.54r et 54v est caractérisée par des traits wisigothiques et des neumes d’Aquitaine et orisci catalans ont été notés sur les f.1r et 54v vers la même période.

Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Pal. germ. 807; Part 1: f. 1–63

details.value:
363 prescriptions for various illnesses, in no particular order. Recipe contributors, people on whom the remedies were tested, and informants are not named.

1. Fols. 1v–2v: 16 prescriptions concerning which herbs are used or applied.
2. Fol. 3v: Note: all the entries written in this book are crossed out, not because they are wrong or objectionable, but because they are all written elsewhere in another book. The lines are marked so that what is written here should not be written again. Marginal note: “Note.”
3. Fols. 4r–7v: 28 recipes for diseases of the mouth, throat, and teeth.
4. Fols. 8r–10v: 17 plague recipes. Heading: “For the pestilence.”
5. Fols. 11v–12v: 10 recipes for erysipelas / “rose.”
6. Fols. 13r–15v: 24 recipes for various illnesses: fever, dysentery or “red belly,” abdominal pain, poisoning.
7. Fols. 16r/v: 9 recipes for coughs and chest ailments.
8. Fols. 17r–18v: 16 recipes for diseases of the body and abdomen.
9. Fols. 18v–23r: 29 recipes for various illnesses: headache, dizziness, hallucinations, stomach problems, liver problems, abscesses, blood purification, stroke.
10. Fols. 24r–29v: 40 recipes for women’s illnesses.
11. Fols. 30r–31v: 15 recipes for jaundice and dropsy.
12. Fols. 32r–34r: 19 recipes for various illnesses: stone, stroke, epilepsy, fever, and other conditions.
13. Fols. 34v–35r: 11 recipes for the ears.
14. Fol. 35v: 6 recipes for the eyes.
15. Fols. 36r/v: 6 recipes against wounds.
16. Fols. 37r–38r: 15 recipes against various illnesses, including worms in the stomach, colic, rage, and heart pain.
17. Fols. 38r–39v: 17 recipes for teeth and gums.
18. Fols. 39v–44v: 36 recipes for various diseases, including cancer or boils, fistulas, scabies, spots, etc.
19. Fols. 45v–47v: 12 recipes for wounds.
20. Fols. 48r–53r: 35 recipes for various illnesses and cosmetics.
21. Fols. 54r–56v: 11 recipes for edema, sores, ruptures, and scabies.
22. Fols. 57v–58r: Sage tract, not in Hlawitschka. Heading: “How one should make the water of virtues, this drink of youth…”
23. Fols. 58r–62r: 10 recipes for various illnesses, especially stomach, head, and wounds.
24. Fols. 62v–63r: Index. Alphabetical list of indications in Latin and German, referring to fols. 4–61, equivalent to modern fols. 1–58.
25. Fol. 63r: At the upper margin, beginning of a recipe: “For the swelling under the…” It breaks off.

Fols. 3r, 11r, 23v, 45r, 53v, 55v, 57r, 58v, and 63v are blank.
Master Stefan, preacher at St Peter’s: medical recipe collection

details.value: Henrieta of Lathilliaco, Lathilliacum, Colophon, High, Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, BnF Latin 11969, Hugo Ripelin, Compendium theologicae veritatis, written between the lines and on the margins of a codex containing biblical texts from the 12th century. The space intended for the gloss, which was left blank, was occupied by the new text. The dimensions of the manuscript (ff.195) are 320x215 mm, the space for the original text is 208x90 mm for 18 lines on a full page. Many of the sheets were partially cut, presumably to make parchment. In 1354, before the new text was added, the codex had belonged to Nicasius, curate of 'Casiacum' (Chezy-sur-Marne, Aisne), as can be deduced from the ex libris on f.195v.The manuscript was later transferred to Saint-Germain-des-Prés (ex libris of the 16th century on f.195v and of the 18th century, with the signature 116, on the unnumbered sheet preceding f.1).

value.title: Anonymous, TBC, Medical Recipes
Iustina a lupffen, Female, Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Pal. germ. 807, f. 1-63

details.value:
363 prescriptions for various illnesses, in no particular order. Recipe contributors, people on whom the remedies were tested, and informants are not named.

1. Fols. 1v–2v: 16 prescriptions concerning which herbs are used or applied.
2. Fol. 3v: Note: all the entries written in this book are crossed out, not because they are wrong or objectionable, but because they are all written elsewhere in another book. The lines are marked so that what is written here should not be written again. Marginal note: “Note.”
3. Fols. 4r–7v: 28 recipes for diseases of the mouth, throat, and teeth.
4. Fols. 8r–10v: 17 plague recipes. Heading: “For the pestilence.”
5. Fols. 11v–12v: 10 recipes for erysipelas / “rose.”
6. Fols. 13r–15v: 24 recipes for various illnesses: fever, dysentery or “red belly,” abdominal pain, poisoning.
7. Fols. 16r/v: 9 recipes for coughs and chest ailments.
8. Fols. 17r–18v: 16 recipes for diseases of the body and abdomen.
9. Fols. 18v–23r: 29 recipes for various illnesses: headache, dizziness, hallucinations, stomach problems, liver problems, abscesses, blood purification, stroke.
10. Fols. 24r–29v: 40 recipes for women’s illnesses.
11. Fols. 30r–31v: 15 recipes for jaundice and dropsy.
12. Fols. 32r–34r: 19 recipes for various illnesses: stone, stroke, epilepsy, fever, and other conditions.
13. Fols. 34v–35r: 11 recipes for the ears.
14. Fol. 35v: 6 recipes for the eyes.
15. Fols. 36r/v: 6 recipes against wounds.
16. Fols. 37r–38r: 15 recipes against various illnesses, including worms in the stomach, colic, rage, and heart pain.
17. Fols. 38r–39v: 17 recipes for teeth and gums.
18. Fols. 39v–44v: 36 recipes for various diseases, including cancer or boils, fistulas, scabies, spots, etc.
19. Fols. 45v–47v: 12 recipes for wounds.
20. Fols. 48r–53r: 35 recipes for various illnesses and cosmetics.
21. Fols. 54r–56v: 11 recipes for edema, sores, ruptures, and scabies.
22. Fols. 57v–58r: Sage tract, not in Hlawitschka. Heading: “How one should make the water of virtues, this drink of youth…”
23. Fols. 58r–62r: 10 recipes for various illnesses, especially stomach, head, and wounds.
24. Fols. 62v–63r: Index. Alphabetical list of indications in Latin and German, referring to fols. 4–61, equivalent to modern fols. 1–58.
25. Fol. 63r: At the upper margin, beginning of a recipe: “For the swelling under the…” It breaks off.

Fols. 3r, 11r, 23v, 45r, 53v, 55v, 57r, 58v, and 63v are blank.
Master Stefan, preacher at St Peter’s: medical recipe collection

details.value:
Janneken Tijers, Deventer, Colophon, High, Deventer, Athenaeumbibliotheek, 101 A 34 KL, Five sheets with writing exercises by Deventer girls, one of them dated 1586. The texts are probably copies of Deventer archive documents. Sheet a: Two writing exercises by Alijt van Hyell (?). - page b: Two writing exercises by Elsa Luickens (?). - page c: Writing exercise (copy of charter mayors, aldermen and council of Deventer) by Jenneken van Brijell (?). - page d: Writing exercise by Janneken Tijers (?). - page e: Writing exercise by Maria van Appeldoorn
Paper, 5 sheets (2 folded and 3 cut), sheet a: 395×273 mm, sheet b: 444×320 mm, sheets ce (cut): 195×315 mm. - At least two leaves served as maculature

details.value:
Dis bůch het uns geton schriben die erwirdig junckfrow Johanna von Mersperck in dem jor do man zalt von Christi gebůrt m° cccc° xxviij. 
Johanna (Jeanne) von Mörsberg may be regarded either as the scribe of this manuscript or as its commissioner, since tůn schriben can also mean “to have [something] written.” A Poor Clare at the convent of Gnadenthal in Basel, she became, in 1430, a penitent at St Mary Magdalene in the convent “An den Steinen,” where she died in 1450 (?) (Degler-Spengler).

Jouarre Laud 1, Ascribed to Chelles by Bischoff, to Jouarre by McKitterick., Low, Oxford, Bodleian Library, Laud misc 126, Can't be consulted (restricted)
At least fifteen hands.
(note: Jouarre was a double monastery, so these scribes could be women or men)
Origin North France, doubtless Chelles. The peculiar uncial and the decoration connect this MS with the group represented by the famous Sacramentary, Vatic. Regin. Lat. 316 (CLA 1.105). On f.1 is added in Anglo-Saxon script saec. VIII–IX Charlemagne's Letter to Abbot Baugulf of Fulda, and on f.260 a library catalogue, perhaps of Würzburg (see CLA plate). Belonged to St Kilian's of Würzburg certainly by the ninth century, as is shown by the entry on f.1v ('. . . faciat eum sancto Kiliano restitui'). The same page has the Würzburg ex-libris saec. XIII. Acquired by Archbishop Laud before 1638.
Ascribed to Chelles by Bischoff, to Jouarre by McKitterick.

details.value:
Justina Blarer, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

details.value: Katarina Gudmundsdotter (Gudmundi), Vadstena, Palaeography analaysis, Low

Linköping City Library, T 229, This manuscript was written in Vadstena Abbey, in the nuns scriptorium. The parchment was payed by sr Birgitta Gudmundi and it was completed at S Michaels eve 1517. It was written by one of the nuns, keeping her identity secret in the colophon on f.37v. It contained music and was intended for use in the church. There are closely related manuscripts in both Uppsala and Stockholm Libraries, either written or decorated by the same nun/nuns. The nuns had taken influence from their sisters i the Netherlands in the design of the large pen-flourished initials. One of the nuns who most frequently painted her large decorated initials in the same style as here was Christina Hansdotter Brask, but she seem to have hade successors. A very similar design can be found in KB A 12, UUB C 431, C 443, C 484, RA E 9002. Some of these are by Christina Hansdotter Brask and from the same period as this manuscript. The present mss is however executed by a much more stable hand than the Brask mss from the same period. A more suitable candidate is Katarina Gudmundsdotter, whose palaeography is in accordance with the scribe of this mss.

details.value: Katharina Konnygs, Hamm, Colophon, High, Düsseldorf, Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek , B 38, The colophon on page 233 r proves that it was written in 1473 by three nuns. Although the fonts change, the text sections of these three writers can be identified according to their writings (see above). Their names were entered in the necrology of the Cistercian monastery in Kentrop (Berlin SB Ms. lat. qu. 297) in the late 15th century: Katharina de Westhoven on October 28th (page 34 r ), Anna Kyttelers on March 15th (page 34 ). . 15 r ) and Katharina Konnygs (Regis) on May 7th (page 19 v ):

details.value:
Katharina von Karpfen, Villingen, Colophon, High, Einsiedeln, Stiftsbibliothek , Ms. 652, 1524/78

f.1 posessionmark: "Miner hertzliben sch. Kunigunda von mir schw. Maria Cleopha Duocherin im gotzhuss zuo sant Clara in Filingen, butt dich, min hertzlieben schw(ester), wellest gott och fu"r mich bitten, das selbe will ich och thun, diewil ietz leb, damit sind gott befolchen, den 15. tag abrilis 6011 ( = 1611). Under this is another hand: "Dis ho"rtt dem gotzhus santt Petter in Schwitz." (SMAH V/152)
f.1
(Possession note):My dearest Sister Kunigunda, from me, Sister Maria Cleopha Duocherin, in the convent of Saint Clare in Villingen: I beg you, my dearest sister, please also pray to God for me — that I will also do, as long as I live. With this, may we both be entrusted to God, on the 15th day of April, 1611.
(In another hand below)
This belongs to the convent of Saint Peter in Schwyz.

details.value:
Klara Keiperin, Nuremberg, Colophon, High, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 33, Parchment is used for f.s 1, 156-157, 230, 265-266, 277-278, and consistently for the outer double leaf of each quire.
cursive book script by three different hands:
 1. f.s 7r-145v, 164r-225v, 227r-257v by Kunigund Niklasin.
 2. f.s 2r-4v, 148r-158r, 171r-v, 226r-v, 230r-v, 258r-281v, and fragments at 5r and 289r by Klara Keiperin.
 3. Later additions at the end of the 15th or early 16th century (282r after the text).

Copied by Kunigund Niklasin and Klara Keiperin from a book borrowed from the convent by a virgin named Anna Winterin, which was later passed to Margareta Scheurerin in Pforzheim.

Of the original three-volume work (previously signed E I–III), only this second volume has survived.

Le nom de l'écrivain be peut pas être déterminé ici de manière tout à fait objective. Dans la deuxième partie, le nom du scribe est certain, mais l'époque n'est pas assez précise. Cependant en 1486, Anna Fickesdotter devint prieure et cela aurait probablement été mentionné d'une manière ou d'une autre si le manuscrit avait été écrit après cette années. Mais il ne fait aucun doute que la main est la même dans les deux parties. Kristina Johansdotter Brask a écrit le directorium chori.

details.value:
Kunigund Niklasin, Nuremberg, Colophon, High, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 33, Parchment is used for f.s 1, 156-157, 230, 265-266, 277-278, and consistently for the outer double leaf of each quire.
cursive book script by three different hands:
 1. f.s 7r-145v, 164r-225v, 227r-257v by Kunigund Niklasin.
 2. f.s 2r-4v, 148r-158r, 171r-v, 226r-v, 230r-v, 258r-281v, and fragments at 5r and 289r by Klara Keiperin.
 3. Later additions at the end of the 15th or early 16th century (282r after the text).

Copied by Kunigund Niklasin and Klara Keiperin from a book borrowed from the convent by a virgin named Anna Winterin, which was later passed to Margareta Scheurerin in Pforzheim.

Of the original three-volume work (previously signed E I–III), only this second volume has survived.

Kunigund Schreiberin, Nuremberg, Unclear, Low, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 14, 2 hands:

2nd hand: f.205ra–307vb.
Later additions by two further hands:
1st: f.301r–v,

“Item in this book are found first the 24 harps… then about Saint Catherine of Siena.”

On f.1r: Swester Kungund Clos Schryberin (Sister Kunigund Clos, scribe); see also IV,6.

Brought into the convent by Kunigund Schreiberin (MBK III, 3, p. 615).

details.value:
Kunigund Schreiberin, Nuremberg, Colophon. Is this Kunigund Niklasin?, Low, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 37, Contains addenda written on f.129v-131v in the monastery of St. Katharina Nuremberg, including a text on f.130-131v with a note by the Kunigund scribe
Is this Kunigund Niklasin?

Gothic cursive script by several hands:
	•	Hand 1: fols. 1r–93r and 127r–129v
	•	Hand 2: fols. 93r–124v
	•	Hand 3: f.129v
	•	Hand 4: fols. 130r–131v, the hand of the scribe Kunigund, as seen on f.131v:
“Küngünt Schreyberin scripsit do pit got für mit einem avemaria dez begert sy daz irgotgnedig sey.”
(“Küngünt the scribe wrote [this]; she asks God with a Hail Mary that He may be merciful to her.”)
Hands 3 and 4 are additions, written in the Katharinenkloster.

details.value: Loppa von Spiegel, Cologne, Script comparison, Medium, London, Victoria and Albert Museum, Inv.-Nr. 8997 I, An Antiphonal contains the choral parts sung during the celebration of the Divine Office or Mass celebrated by a monastic or other community. This type of choirbook was usually written in large format so that the whole choir could read the music at once. This example was made at the convent of St Klara in Cologne by one of the nuns, Sister Loppa de Speculo. Another surviving leaf records that Sister Jutta paid for the book while Loppa carried out the writing, lining (putting in the staves for the music), notation and illumination 'in the year 1350, when there was a great plague everywhere'. This was one of a series of books produced in the convent. The Abbess, Heylwigis von Beechoven, who had ruled the convent since 1344, is portrayed kneeling by the historiated initial of the Descent of the Holy Ghost on the Virgin and Apostles associating her prayer with this crucial event, when the Holy Spirit came to earth and the mission of the Apostles to spread the Christian revelation began. The prayer of her convent was thus part of the mission.

details.value:
1. Fols. 1r–12r – Office of the Dead
2. Fols. 12r–13v – Bernardine of Siena: Prayer on the Name of Jesus
3. Fols. 14r–17r – Blessing of the Candle on Holy Saturday (from the Mass liturgy)
4. Fols. 17v–65v – Office of the Virgin Mary (German)
5. Fols. 65v–67r – Liturgical Prayers (Latin)
6. Fols. 67v–70v – ‘St Bernard’s Eight Verses’ with Prayers
7. Fols. 70v–71v – ‘Mary Magdalene’s Prayer’
8. Fols. 71v–72r – Advent Prayer
9. Fols. 73r–v – Six Spiritual Teachings
10. Fols. 73v–74r – Christ Teaches Seven Reflections
11. Fols. 74r–v – Hermannus Contractus: Alma redemptoris mater (German)
12. Fols. 75r–78r – ‘St Bernard’s Eight Verses’ with Prayers
13. Fols. 78r–88v – Communion Prayers
14. Fols. 89r–91r – Bernardine of Siena: Prayer on the Name of Jesus
15. Fols. 91r–96v – Prayers to St Bernardine of Siena
All in German

details.value:
Margarete Kartäuserin, Nuremberg, Script comparison, Medium, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 18, Two-column layout, book cursive script by various hands:
 1. 1r-54vb, 260ra-268vb: Hand of Kunigund Niklasin.
 2. 33ra-34rb, 102ra-117vb.
 3. 55ra-67vb, 81vb-82va, 153ra-166vb, 186ra-1862ra.
 4. 68r.
 5. 68va-81vb.
 6. 83ra-85rb, 219ra-232vb: Hand of Margareta, a Carthusian.
 7. 85rb-101vb, 186ra-218rb.
 8. 118ra-152vb: Hand of Barbara Rutzin.
 9. 233ra-246vb.
 10. 246vb-259vb.

Often written quire by quire; when one hand finishes, the remaining part of the quire is left blank or the blank f.s are cut out.

details.value:
Margarete Kartäuserin, Nuremberg, Colophon, High, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. V App. 34p, Fols. 1r of Vol. 1 and f.4r of Vol. 2 decorated by the nun Barbara Gwichtmacherin from the Katharinenkloster (cf.Fischer, Buchmalerei, p. 74f., fig. 29; Schneider, op. cit., p. XXf.).
Comparative analysis of the remaining historiated initials suggests attribution to five different artists, though Fischer proposes only four illuminators (op. cit., p. 79f.).

Colophon on front cover: Anno Domini 1459, this book was bound in honor of our Lord Jesus Christ and the most holy Virgin Mary, and the glorious virgin and martyr Catherine, by brothers Wilhelm Krug and Johannes Wirsing, of the Order of Preachers.

details.value:
Maria Dies de Oña, Burgos, Colophon, High, Dallas, Bridwell Library, Southern Methodist University, BRMS 155, Produced, signed, and dated by the Spanish nun Maria Dies de Oña, this early sixteenth-century Spanish manuscript gradual contains the “propers” and choral chants for the Mass for Cistercian Use, according to the pre-Tridentine liturgical calendar. Although a complete volume, it is not a complete work as it contains approximately only the first third of the liturgical year, from the first Sunday in Advent to Palm Sunday. Given the size and format of this volume, the complete gradual for the entire liturgical year would have been represented by three or four volumes.

Produced by a female religious copyist for use by the female monastery of San Salvador de Oña in Burgos, this substantial volume is almost entirely composed of chant and does not include the long spoken portions of the Mass. Minor leaf repairs, occasional corrections, marginal additions, and instructions for following the text indicate that this manuscript was used on a regular basis.

details.value:
Maria Horn, Boppard, Colophon, High, Fulda, Landesbibliothek, Ms. Aa 125, The origin in a Franciscan convent is evidenced by:
	•	The feast of the stigmatization of St. Francis (135r) and the rubric on f.150r referring to von unßerm werdigen vader Franciscus (“our worthy Father Francis”).
	•	The suffrage for Severus, unserm Patrone (“our patron”) on f.162r, situated within the liturgical year sequence between November 11 and November 21, suggesting Boppard (Archdiocese of Trier).
In 1489, Franciscan sisters from Besselich settled in Boppard, known for their manuscript production (cf.J. Marx, Geschichte des Erzstifts Trier, vol. 2, part 2, 1862, p. 423, and K. Schlegel, Besselich am Mittelrhein, 1980, p. 19).

details.value:
Maria van Appeldoorn, Deventer, Colophon, High, Deventer, Athenaeumbibliotheek, 101 A 34 KL, Five sheets with writing exercises by Deventer girls, one of them dated 1586. The texts are probably copies of Deventer archive documents. Sheet a: Two writing exercises by Alijt van Hyell (?). - page b: Two writing exercises by Elsa Luickens (?). - page c: Writing exercise (copy of charter mayors, aldermen and council of Deventer) by Jenneken van Brijell (?). - page d: Writing exercise by Janneken Tijers (?). - page e: Writing exercise by Maria van Appeldoorn
Paper, 5 sheets (2 folded and 3 cut), sheet a: 395×273 mm, sheet b: 444×320 mm, sheets ce (cut): 195×315 mm. - At least two leaves served as maculature

details.value:
A single added f.at the end of Edinburgh University Library, MS 59 that may with certainty be attributed to Mary.

details.value:
Mouwersdochter, Naarden, Colophon, High, Amsterdam, Universiteitsbibliotheek Amsterdam, XV E 21, (ff.1; 8-9; 198-199)
[Apparamment il faut comprendre que Sustef a préparé le livre pour Fye. Au f.9v°, elle donnait les obits de son père, d'un frère et d'une sœur (1467-1477); plus tard (?) elle (?) ajoutait ceux de l'oncle Ansse (1468; sans doute le père de Fye), de deux autres frères (1468, 1481) et les noms d'une sœur et de Suster elle-même (ces deux étant encore en vie). Une autre main (celle de Fye?) a noté le décès de ces deux dernières (1509, 1510) ainsi que d'une autre personne de la famille (1519).]

Ursulenhuis, 101 F 15 KL, copied in 1459 in the Brandeshuis and 101 F 3 KL, copied in 1464 by a sister in the Kerstekenshuis or Brandeshuis, the predecessors of the S. Ursulenhuis., Low

Ursulenhuis, 101 F 15 KL, copied in 1459 in the Brandeshuis and 101 F 3 KL, copied in 1464 by a sister in the Kerstekenshuis or Brandeshuis, the predecessors of the S. Ursulenhuis., Low

Horarium with prayers in Swedish (Christina Hansdotter Brask's prayer book)

Title: None

Title: None

Title: None

Title: None

Rubric: On the Holy Cross

Rubric: Hours on the compassion of the Blessed Virgin
It begins: Alas, O Lord, the lips of the sea!

Title: None

Title: None

Heading: Here byrias salutaciones mykit godha
Incipit: I greet you, my lady Mary, the eternal, the most beautiful creature of the Himerikis, the queen.

Title: None

Title: None

Title: None

Title: None
Incipit: My sweetest wife, Mrs. Maria, give me something to think about.

Rubric: The seven psalms begin

Title: None

Title: None

Title: None

details.value: Ms. London Ms.546 Unidentified nun-scribe A, Syon, Colophon, Low, London, Lambeth Palace Library, Ms. 546, Lambeth Palace Library MS 546 is a collection of devotional material written by a number of late fifteenth- or early sixteenth-century hands. The main contents are 'The xv Sorowes of oure lady' (fos 7v-20v) and the 'golden letany' (fos 34r-51v, with a preface on fos 29r-33v),4 with devotions in English, and prayers in English and Latin making up the rest of the volume. It is with one of these devotions, specifically its colophon, that the present note is concerned.

details.value:
Incipit (text): Gli stati ne quali conversano li virtuose creature sonno multi (fol. 1r)
Incipit (text): Con ciò sia cosa che più volte et in diversi tempi (fol. 13r)
Incipit (text): Perch’io fui più volte da multe et sancte creature per la loro devotione (fol. 15v)
Incipit (text): A le venerabile spirituali religiose et sancte donne (fol. 20v)
Incipit (text): Hoc enim sentite in vobis (fol. 22v)
Incipit (text): Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde (fol. 24r)
Incipit (text): Considerando i secreti inganni i quali i servi di Cristo recevono (fol. 28r)
Incipit (text): Le spirationi sono quasi infinite et sono multi gli spiratori (fol. 32v)
Incipit (text): In genesi dicitur faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram (fol. 34r)
Incipit (text): El primo si è usare el cose temporali vile et disprezzare (fol. 35r)
Incipit (text): Al suo in Cristo sé medismo etc. Considerando la profonda humilità (fol. 35v)
Incipit (text): Volendo Cristo che nullo si possa di sua imperfectione scusare (fol. 38r)

The manuscript is composed of partially incomplete prayer booklets written by various hands at different times. The initial section was written in 1496 at the Benedictine Monastery of Lorch: “56v Written in Lorch in the year 1496 by Clemens of the convent brothers of Lorch” (likely Clemens Aurifabri, prior in 1490; see Württembergische Geschichtsquellen, Vol. 12, 1910, p. 86).

details.value:
Incipit (text): Gli stati ne quali conversano li virtuose creature sonno multi (fol. 1r)
Incipit (text): Con ciò sia cosa che più volte et in diversi tempi (fol. 13r)
Incipit (text): Perch’io fui più volte da multe et sancte creature per la loro devotione (fol. 15v)
Incipit (text): A le venerabile spirituali religiose et sancte donne (fol. 20v)

Incipit (text): El primo si è usare el cose temporali vile et disprezzare (fol. 35r)
Incipit (text): Al suo in Cristo sé medismo etc. Considerando la profonda humilità (fol. 35v)
Incipit (text): Volendo Cristo che nullo si possa di sua imperfectione scusare (fol. 38r)

details.value: Regina Sattler, St. Gallen, Colophon, High, St.Gallen, Stiftsbibliothek , Ms. Sang. 603, Manuscrit composite du XVe siècle, en provenance du couvent dominicain Sainte-Catherine à Saint-Gall. Le codex composé de cinq fascicules reliés, en langue allemande, contient en plus d'un traité sur la Passion (« Les quarante bouquets de myrrhe de la Passion du Christ »), l'histoire de la fondation du couvent dominicain de Sainte-Catherine à Diessenhofen, le livre des sœurs de Diessenhofen et de Tösser, les légendes d'Elisabeth de Hongrie, de Marguerite de Hongrie, d'Ida de Toggenburg et de Louis de Toulouse, ainsi qu'un court extrait du Liber specialis gratiae de Mechthild von Hackeborn en traduction allemande. (fas)

details.value:
Regula Keller, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

details.value: Regula Keller, St. Gallen, Colophon, High, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, M 32, After the council of the city of St. Gallen lifted the enclosure of the Dominican monastery of St. Catherine on May 2, 1528, and the convent gradually dissolved, only Regula Keller and two sisters remained in the monastery buildings, where she continued to copy the Rule of Augustine and the Constitutions of the Order of Preachers until 1543. The reading of the Rule and Constitutions was emphasized more strongly in Reformed monasteries, in keeping with the nature of the Observance. (men)

details.value:
Regula Keller, St. Gallen, Unclear, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, No inventory number, Main hand and accounting entries written by Prioress Anna Krumm, e.g., fols. 1r–2r [1v blank], ljrv, lxiijr–lxviv, and throughout
 • Alternating with the hand of Angela Varnbühler, in semi-cursive; both using brown ink
 • f.lxxiiijv: a 7-line entry in almost black ink by Elisabeth Schaigenwiler
 • Additional hands from around 1450, including some otherwise unknown female scribes

Numerous marginal annotations by Regula Keller in the first half of the 16th century (ca. 1530 and after), using a very fine quill
 • Examples:
 • f.1r: “The estates were sold during the adversities of the Lutheran times by the people of St. Gallen”
 • f.4v: “The estate was also sold in the turbulent Lutheran times by the people of St. Gallen”
 • f.11r: “The estate was sold by the people of St. Gallen as they authorized us”
(see also fig. 25)

details.value:
Sapientia Wirt, St. Gallen, Script comparison, Medium, Wil, Dominikarinnenkloster St. Katharina, Chronik ("Konventsbuch"), Ce manuscrit, qui dans la recherche scientifique antérieure a souvent été appelé « Chronique », est le « Konventsbuch » de St. Katharina à Saint-Gall (61r:...und sol dis also in des convents buoch gesetz werden...). On y trouve des entrées chronologiques concernant les intérêts économiques du couvent. Le manuscrit a été établi au cours de la réforme au moment où le couvent passait de propriété privée à une propriété commune. Ainsi, ce livre permettait à la direction du couvent de St. Katharina de rendre compte auprès de la communauté des possessions gérées. Il permettait également aux sœurs de connaître l’état de leurs biens initialement déposés au couvent. Le manuscrit contient des contributions concernant les activités de construction, l’équipement, le scriptorium, les contentieux, les donations, mais aussi des entrées relatives à certaines soeurs, directeurs de conscience ou ouvriers, ainsi que, épisodiquement, des entrées concernant l’histoire du couvent.
 The chronicle contains reports and notes from a wide variety of areas of contemporary convent history: Angela Varnbühler 's investing hand begins (ex post) with her election as prioress in 1476, and continues with a list of the conventuals as well as reports from the implementation of the first Steps to reform the monastery. The other entries, in chronological order, concern a wide variety of events from everyday convent life: entry of novices and their later profession; News of death (from conventuals, relatives and friends); Endowments (of seasons and interest) and gifts; Book production in the scriptorium; Economy of the monastery (conductor's annual accounts, administration, land acquisition [fields, forests, vineyards]); Expansion and conversion as well as artistic furnishings of the monastery buildings; Contemporary events from the history of the monastery and order - even the event of the solar eclipse in 1485 found its way into the chronicle with an entry by the prioress (f.45r ).

Their own hands, or those from their immediate environment, can be found in a total of 10 other Lamspringer Codices: 443 Helmst. , 447 Helmst. , 482a Helmst. (1r-81v), 510 Helmst. , 511 Helmst. , 519 Helmst. , 718 Helmst. (10v-97r), 723 Helmst. , 903 Helmst. (1r-75r), 943 Helmst. and 1030 Helmst. (on the separation of hands and the group, see Härtel Written and Painted , 21f.). 

Carolino-Gothica by the hand of the Scriptrix (belonging to the group: 443 Helmst. , 447 Helmst. , 482a [1r-81v], 510 Helmst. , 511 Helmst. , 519 Helmst. , 718 Helmst. [10v-97r], 723 Helmst. , 903 Helmst. [1r-75r], 1030 Helmst .
Characteristic of the Scriptrix group are the extraordinarily numerous and varied initial majuscules in the present manuscript, mostly decorated with dots, which have feather-like palmettes, mythical creature heads, bud, leaf and flower motifs in the trimmings and are occasionally filled with simple wavy lines.

details.value:
Sophia, Marienberg, Colophon, High, Wolfenbüttel, Herzog August Bibliothek, Cod. Guelf. 502 Helmst., During the period in which the Hs. was created, four bearers of this name have been handed down among the Marienberg choir women: the sexton Sophia Barnstorf and the conventual nuns Sophia von Braunschweig , Sophia von Werle and Sophia von Meinersen 
Around 1510, the Graduale was supplemented (Part II) and then re-bound after identifying the scribe's hand and the binding stamp in the Benedictine monastery of Clus in accordance with the requirements of the reformed liturgy of the Bursfeld Benedictine Congregation. 

In the catalogue of Colophons of the Bouveret, noted as wolfenbüttel 542.

Easter Orationale , hymnic meditations on liturgical texts of the Easter season, predominantly in Latin and Low German

details.value:
Prayer book:
 • 57r–71r: Passion prayers beginning “Protect me at all times and especially at my last departure…” including (on 59r) a list of saints predominantly of Dominican origin.
70r: Morning prayer addressed to Eternal Wisdom: “O most beautiful, most radiant, eternal Wisdom…”
 • 71v–83v: Prayers to saints including Mary Magdalene, (76r) Anna, (78r) George, (79r) Nicholas, (80r) Dorothea, (80v) Barbara, (81v) Margaret, (82v) Catherine. At 83v, the date mentioned earlier is repeated.
 • 88r–100v: Prayer by St. Bernard when Jesus descended to him from the Cross: “Hail, Jesus, the salvation of the world…”
 • 101r: Blank.
 • 101v: Rubric for the Rosary of Christ, incomplete.
 • 142r–153v: Exhortation for the contemplation of the sovereignty of God, German, ,

details.value:
Ursula Geiselherin, Nuremberg, Script comparison, Medium, Nuremberg, Stadtbibliothek, Cent. IV 30, The ms. bore the signature E LXIII in Nuremberg's St. Catherine's Monastery .
Continuation in Nuremberg, Stadtbibl., Cod. Cent. V, 5
written in book cursive by the hand of Ursula Geiselherin; a second hand appears on f.s 185rb-189ra, 217vb-219rb; corrections and additions by a third hand.

Written by Ursula Geiselherin based on an exemplar from the Klarakloster (Poor Clares) in Nuremberg.

The exemplar is preserved in Berlin, germ. f.1276 (see Degering I, p. 171), formerly Cheltenham, Phillipps 19491 (see Priebsch, Deutsche Handschriften in England I (1896), p. 127, no. 131).

The copy made at the Katharinenkloster is in two volumes; Volume II = Cent. V, 5.
